chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

We went to him as a group and said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! We intend to go to Iraq, so advise us.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Let your strong ones strengthen your weak ones, and let your rich ones assist your poor ones, and do not divulge our secret nor broadcast our matter. And whenever a hadith comes to you from us, and you find a witness or two witnesses for it from the Book of Allah, then take it; otherwise, pause with it, then refer it back to us until it becomes clear to you.'

And know that the one awaiting this matter has a reward like that of the fasting one who stands (in night prayer). And whoever catches up with our Qa'im and goes out with him and kills our enemy, for him is a reward like that of twenty martyrs. And whoever is killed with our Qa'im, for him is a reward like that of twenty-five martyrs.

key_terms.الْمُنْتَظِرُ: The one awaiting (the reappearance of the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for those who await the Qa'im and fight with him according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi’s chapter on Occultation, this hadith outlines the protocol for the Shia community during the Minor and Major Ghaybah, emphasizing communal solidarity, preserving the secret of the Imam, and verifying reports against the Quran. It further underscores the eschatological significance of 'Intizar' (awaiting), equating the patience of those waiting for the Qa'im with the reward of continuous fasting and prayer.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘We went over to him<sup>asws</sup> as a group, so we said, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!

We want (to go to) Al-Iraq, so advise us’. So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Let your strong ones strengthen your weak ones, and let your rich ones assist your poor ones, and neither divulge our<sup>asws</sup> secrets nor broadcast our<sup>asws</sup> matter. And, whenever a Hadeeth comes to you from us<sup>asws</sup>, and you find a proof over it, or two proofs from the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, then take with it, or else, pause during it, then refer it back to us<sup>asws</sup> until it is clarified for you.

And know that the one awaiting for this matter (rising of Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup>), for him would be a Recompense like for the Fasting one (during the day), the standing one (for the Salat during the night). And the one who comes across our<sup>asws</sup> Qaim<sup>asws</sup>, so he goes out with him<sup>asws</sup> and kills our<sup>asws</sup> enemies, for him would be a Recompense like for twenty martyrs. And the one who is killed with our<sup>asws</sup> Qaim<sup>asws</sup>, would have for him a Recompense like for twenty five martyrs’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from a man who has said the following: “

Once we in a group went to see abu Ja’far (a.s.) and said to him, ‘O descendent of the Messenger of Allah, we intend to travel to Iraq, and request your recommendations.’ Abu Ja’far (a.s.) said, ‘The stronger ones among you must support the weak ones, the well to do among you must reach out to the poor ones among you, do not expose our secrets and do not publicize our cause. When you receive a Hadith from us accept it only if you find sufficient, two or at least one, supporting evidence from the book of Allah, otherwise, keep it on hold and then refer it to us for verification.

You must know that those waiting for this matter (coming of Imam al-Mahdi) have a reward like those who fast all the time and pray every night. Whoever will find himself with our al-Qa’im (al-Mahdi) and will come out with him to do away with our enemies he will have a reward equal to that for twenty martyrs and whoever will be killed supporting our al- Qa’im, his reward will be equal to that for fifteen martyrs.’”
